method: Authored teaching notes checked against Stockfish 17.1. Fixed-answer and Maia-favourite searches start from the same root position; scores are from the root mover perspective. Search target20/time cap5seconds, Threads1 Hash64; the replacement uses depth22. Actual depths and mate scores are retained. Teaching illustrations are curated, separate from the random research audit. Replay excerpts include all moves cited in the notes; full searched lines remain here.

items.title: Keep a defender for d6
items.why: The knight on b5 is attacking Black’s bishop on d6. Retreating to b7 puts Black’s knight in position to recapture: the line reaches Nxd6 Nxd6, preventing White from winning a bishop. Black can then push the b-pawn toward promotion instead of losing a bishop during the race.
items.alternative: Maia’s first choice, ...a2, rushes the passer forward but leaves Nxd6 unanswered by a knight. White can follow with Nb5 and d6, gaining counterplay while Black tries to recover the lost bishop.
items.notice: Before pushing a passed pawn, check which of your pieces can be taken with tempo.

items.title: Connect the rooks before taking c4
items.why: Move the d8-rook first: it is relying on the c8-rook for protection. After ...Rd7, Black can double on the c-file with ...Rdc7 and bring the f8-knight out through d7. That keeps the pieces working together against c4.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Rxc4 removes the defender of d8. White answers Rxd8; Black’s ...Rxf4 takes a knight, but gives up a rook in return.
items.notice: A tempting capture can uncover an attack on the piece your rook was defending.

items.title: Enter through the f-file
items.why: The f-file gives Black a direct route to White’s back rank. ...Rf8 attacks the bishop on f1; after Be2, ...Rf2 attacks it again and Re1 ties a rook to its defence. Black then takes h2, keeping both bishops and an active rook.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...b4 leads to Bg2 Bxd3+ Kxd3: Black wins an exchange, but White’s king reaches d3. In that line, c4 supports White’s passed d-pawn, and the engine prefers White’s position.
items.notice: Look for a file that lets your rook attack successive targets.

items.title: The promotion threat protects the queen
items.why: ...dxe3 takes the knight even though White’s rook can take the queen on c5. After Rxc5, Black has ...exf2+ and then ...fxe1=B+, capturing White’s queen as the pawn promotes. White therefore plays f3 in the main line, and Black saves the queen with ...Qb6 while keeping the extra piece.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Qb6 saves the queen immediately, but gives the attacked knight time to escape to c4. Black misses the chance to take it with the promotion threat in reserve.
items.notice: Before saving an attacked queen, calculate forcing pawn captures near the enemy king.

items.title: Trade queens to escape the mating net
items.why: Black is already a knight down, and the exposed king makes the queens dangerous. ...Qf7 offers a trade: after Qxf7+ Kxf7, the immediate mating threats are gone. Black is still losing, but can activate the king and try to create a passed pawn.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...g4 allows Nf6+, threatening Qxh7 mate if the king goes to h8. The line shown instead gives up the queen with ...Qxf6, which loses much faster.
items.notice: In a lost position, removing a mating attack can matter more than starting a pawn race.

items.title: Save the queen and cover a8
items.why: Black is a bishop down, with the queen on d8 and rook on a8 both under attack. ...Qb8 steps out of the f6-bishop’s diagonal while protecting a8 from White’s queen. After Qxd5, ...c6 opens the b8–d6 diagonal, so Black can answer Qxd6+ with ...Qxd6 and get the queens off the board.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Bxh2+ can be met by Kxh2. Black still has to deal with the attack on d8; the line ...Ne6 Bxd8 Rxd8 gives up the queen for a bishop.
items.notice: When two pieces are attacked, look for an escape square that also defends the other piece.

items.title: Make a square for the king
items.why: Moving the g6-pawn to g5 gives the king a retreat square. When White moves the bishop with Bf6+, the queen on c7 gives a discovered check along the seventh rank, and Black can answer ...Kg6. This is a defensive resource in a losing position; White’s h-pawn remains a serious threat.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Nxg7 grabs the bishop but walks into Rh1. The checked continuation is ...g5 Qe7 Kg6 Qf6+ Kh7 hxg7 mate.
items.notice: Before taking a piece beside your king, check the rook’s route to the open file.

items.title: Attack the queen to buy a move
items.why: Black’s king is under heavy pressure, so ...Nf6 develops with an attack on the queen on h5. White’s best reply is Rxf6, taking the knight while keeping the e5-pawn in place to defend d6. Black remains much worse, but ...Rg8 brings the corner rook toward the fight.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...b5 leaves the kingside untouched. White takes g5 with the bishop and then lifts the rook to f3, with a route toward the black king.
items.notice: Look for forcing replies before spending a move away from the attack.

items.title: Close the diagonal, then gain tempi
items.why: ...e6 blocks the b3-bishop’s diagonal toward f7 and covers d5 and f5. When White pushes e5, ...Nh7 moves the attacked knight with a threat against the queen on g5. After Qe3, ...b4 attacks the c3-knight, giving Black time to meet the central advance.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Nxb3 trades away the c5-knight first. After axb3 and ...e6, White has time for f4; later, the queen meets ...Nh7 by entering e7 rather than going back to e3.
items.notice: Combine a defensive pawn move with the threats available after the opponent pushes.

items.title: The check that opens the d-file
items.why: ...Nc3+ forks the king and the rook on d1. Capturing with the bishop would clear the d-file for ...Qxd1 mate, so the main line uses Nxc3 instead. After ...bxc3, Black’s pawn attacks the d2-bishop and takes it after White’s b3.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Qa5 gives White time for b3. When ...Nc3+ finally comes, Bxc3 is safe: the queen has left d8, so the mating trick on d1 is gone.
items.notice: A checking knight sacrifice may work because one recapture uncovers a queen’s line.

items.title: Leave the a6-pawn in place
items.why: The pawn on a6 is keeping a white knight out of b5. ...Rb8 attacks the bishop without moving that pawn; after Bxd7+ Bxd7, Black has developed a bishop and can prepare to castle. Taking the bishop with the pawn would give White a forcing knight jump instead.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...axb5 allows Ndxb5, attacking the queen on c7. After ...Qc6, White takes the d6-pawn with the rook and keeps the initiative.
items.notice: Before taking a bishop, check which knight square your pawn would give up.

items.title: Clear e5 for the other knight
items.why: ...Nf4 attacks the bishop on d3 and the knight on e2. After Bxf4 exf4, Black’s e-pawn has cleared e5 for the knight on d7. That knight lands on e5 and later takes the remaining bishop on d3 in the line shown.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...f4 leaves the pawn on e5 and lets White save the e3-bishop with Bf2. The d7-knight then reroutes through b8 instead of occupying e5.
items.notice: An exchange can improve a second piece by clearing the square it needs.

items.title: Keep a defender for f4
items.why: ...g5 gives the pawn on f4 a defender: a later Bxf4 can be met by ...gxf4. Without that support, the exchanges on e5 leave White able to take f4 without a pawn recapture. White can challenge the new support with h4, so Black still has a difficult position to defend.
items.alternative: After Maia’s ...Bxe5, White has dxe5 ...Rxe5 Bxf4, taking the f4 pawn and developing the bishop. With Black’s g-pawn still on g7, there is no ...gxf4 in reply.
items.notice: Before exchanging on e5, trace the c1–f4 diagonal and check who will defend f4.

items.title: Cover c5 before exchanging knights
items.why: ...Nd7 puts the f6-knight within reach of c5, where Black’s bishop is attacked by the knight on e4. In the displayed line, Black develops the bishop to b7 and returns the knight to d7; Nxc5 can then be answered by ...Nxc5. This is a defensive move in a position where White still has the advantage.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Nxe4 brings White’s queen to e4. After ...f5, Qxc6 ...Qxd3 Qxc5 lets that queen take both the c6 knight and the c5 bishop, while Black recovers only the bishop on d3.
items.notice: After Qxe4, the knight on c6 becomes a target. Check that before removing the knight from f6.

items.title: Block the bishop’s route to c7
items.why: ...e5 closes the f4–e5–d6–c7 diagonal, cutting out Bc7 against the queen on d8. After dxe5, Black has ...Ne4; Nxe4 ...dxe4 trades a pair of knights and leaves White’s own pawn on e5 blocking that bishop. Black can take on c5 later, after dealing with the threat.
items.alternative: The immediate ...bxc5 allows Bc7, followed by ...cxd4 Bxd8. Black has given up the queen; ...dxc3 recovers a knight, but the knight and two captured pawns are insufficient compensation in this line.
items.notice: Look at the bishop on f4 before opening the queenside: c7 is its route into the queen.

items.title: Develop while attacking the queen
items.why: ...Bf5 develops the bishop with an attack on the queen on d3. Qe3 is then met by ...Re8, attacking the queen again along the open e-file. White interposes Ne5 in the line shown, giving Black time for ...Ne4 before White has castled.
items.alternative: Maia’s immediate ...Ne4 lets White castle at once. The line ...Qxc3 Rfe1 shows White getting the king to safety and bringing a rook toward the centre while Black’s bishop is still on c8.
items.notice: The exposed queen on d3 lets Black develop two pieces with consecutive threats.

items.title: Open the queen’s checking diagonal
items.why: ...Bg3+ moves the bishop out of the queen’s way: the queen on g2 now checks the king on e2 through f2. After Kxe3, ...Ng4+ and ...Bf2+ keep the king under check; Qe3+ is answered by ...Bxe3+, taking the queen. The displayed continuation ends in mate.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Nxf1 Rxf1 wins the exchange and also leaves Black much better. It spends the e3 knight on a rook, though, instead of starting the mating attack with a discovered check.
items.notice: The bishop on f2 is blocking its own queen. Moving it can be more forcing than taking the rook.

items.title: Use the threat on the first rank
items.why: ...Rxa5 takes the pawn and offers the rook: Qxa5 is met by ...Qc1+ Nf1 ...Qxb1, recovering the rook on b1. White instead chooses Qd4 in the main line, when ...Qc1+ forces a queen exchange. The rook can then enter on a2 and take the knight on d2, even while White takes pawns with check.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Qc3 allows Rxb7+ first, followed by Qxc3. Black still has a winning position, but White gets a pawn with check and avoids the same immediate pressure on d2.
items.notice: White’s king has few exits. Calculate the checks on c1 before treating the a5 pawn as protected.

items.title: Threaten mate on g2
items.why: ...Qc6 threatens ...Qxg2 mate, with the pawn on h3 protecting g2. White must defend that square or block the diagonal; in this line, R1e2 does the defending. Black then plays ...d3 against the rook on e2 and ...c4 against the queen on b3, advancing both pawns with threats.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...hxg2 gives up the pawn’s support of g2. After Qc4, White has more freedom to attack the centre with f5 instead of answering the mating threat.
items.notice: The h3 pawn is valuable where it stands: it protects the square the queen wants to capture on.

items.title: Bring the queen around to h2
items.why: ...Qf5+ starts a sequence of queen checks: Kg2 ...Qh3+ Kf2 ...Qh2+. Once the queen reaches h2, ...Rf5+ brings the rook into the attack. In the shown line, Qf4 ...Rxf4+ gxf4 ...Qxf4+ costs White the queen for a rook and opens the diagonal from h2 to f4.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Rf5+ is also winning: ...Nc2 forks the queen and rook in the comparison line. Starting with the queen check gives Black the stronger attack rather than settling for that material gain.
items.notice: Follow the route f5–h3–h2. The queen’s final square makes the rook capture on f4 work.

items.title: Answer one attack with another
items.why: The pawn on f3 attacks the knight on g4, but ...Rb8 creates a matching threat against the bishop on b6. After fxg4, ...Rxb6 exchanges that knight for the bishop and brings the rook into play. Black has to calculate the exchange before leaving the knight where it is.
items.alternative: Maia saves the knight with ...Nge5. White then has Rb7, keeping the bishop on b6 and using the seventh rank to put pressure on e7.
items.notice: Before retreating the knight, check whether ...Rb8 gives Black a piece of comparable value in return.

items.title: Keep both bishops in the calculation
items.why: ...Bf6 attacks the queen on g5. After Rxe6, Black can exchange queens through ...Bxg5 Rxc6, then take the bishop on h4; that bishop’s new diagonal also reaches the rook on e1. The displayed sequence ends with ...Bxe1, leaving Black with a rook and bishop against a rook.
items.alternative: After Maia’s ...Rxe3 Rxe3, the same ...Bf6 idea no longer wins a piece. The comparison line simplifies to a bishop ending where White has two extra pawns.
items.notice: Track the bishop through f6, g5, h4 and e1. Exchanging rooks first removes its final target.

items.title: Move the bishop out of the back-rank tactic
items.why: ...Bc6 gets the bishop off a8 before White can open the e-file with a queen exchange. It also gives the bishop a route to e8: in this line, ...Bb5 and ...Be8 put it in front of White’s advanced e6 pawn. Black remains worse, but avoids the immediate loss of that bishop.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...cxb3 allows Qd7 ...Qxd7 exd7. After ...Rd4 axb3 ...Rxd7, Re8+ forces the king away and Rxa8 picks up the bishop left on the back rank.
items.notice: After the e6 pawn captures on d7, the e-file opens all the way to e8. Look beyond the queen exchange.

items.title: Take on f3 with check first
items.why: ...Nxf3+ takes a pawn before Black exchanges queens. After Kh1 ...Qxc2 Nxc2, the knight retreats to g5; Black is still worse, but has won the f3 pawn. Taking the knight with gxf3 instead allows ...Bxd4+ Rxd4 ...Qxc2, as the extra line shows.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Qxb4 lets White chase the queen with Ra4. After ...Qb7, f4 attacks the knight on e5, so White gains time against both pieces.
items.notice: Compare the order: check on f3, exchange queens, then withdraw the knight.

items.title: Clear the bishop’s diagonal
items.why: Nh7 clears f6 for the bishop on e7. Taking the queen with Bxe6 now allows ...Bxg5, pinning White’s queen on f4 to the king on c1; Qxg5 Nxg5 exchanges the queens. White instead chooses Bxe7 in the main line, and ...Qxe7 takes some of the pressure off Black’s king.
items.alternative: Maia prefers ...Qxc4, taking the bishop immediately. Bxf6 then removes the knight, and after ...Kh7 Bxe7 White has taken both minor pieces and keeps the attack going.
items.notice: When a queen is attacked, check whether moving another piece opens a pin against the opposing queen.

items.title: Free the rook and cover f6
items.why: Bd8 adds a defender to the knight on f6 and clears the e-file for the rook on e8. Black can then meet Bd3 with ...Rxe5, giving up the exchange to remove the bishop beside the king. The resulting position is still difficult, but White’s attack loses an important piece.
items.alternative: After Maia’s ...Kg6, Bd3+ sends the king straight back to g7. White then brings the c3-knight through e4 to g3, adding another attacker while Black has spent two moves on the king.

items.title: Retreat outside the queen’s checking line
items.why: Na2 keeps the knight out of reach of Qc2+, while retaining the capture on c3. In the replay it takes White’s c3-knight and later reaches e2 with check. White still has a strong attack, so this retreat is a way to keep fighting rather than a cure for the exposed king.
items.alternative: After Maia’s ...Nb3, Qc2+ checks along the c2–h7 diagonal and attacks the knight on b3. ...Kg8 Qxb3 simply loses that knight.

items.title: Get out of the passed pawn’s way
items.why: Bxb3 clears a2 for Black’s passed pawn. Taking the bishop with Nxb3 allows ...a2 and a dangerous promotion attack; White instead uses Nf6+ to force ...Nxf6 and bring the g-pawn to f6. Black answers with ...g6 and queen checks, reaching a roughly balanced position in this line.
items.alternative: Maia’s ...Qb2+ gives White Kd2 before the bishop moves. In the replay, White can then take the bishop with Nxb3 and use Nf6+ with the king already off the back rank.

items.why: Ref8 prepares ...Rxf3, removing the knight that guards h2. After Rfe1 Rxf3 gxf3, ...Qh2+ brings the queen beside White’s king; the h8-rook can then join it with ...Rf8. Black gives up the exchange for an attack, which is more urgent than another pawn push.

items.why: h5 attacks the bishop on g4 before Black pushes ...e4. After Bxh5 e4, the bishop cannot reach f5 in one move; ...Rh8 soon gains another tempo against it on h5. Black gets activity on the h-file while White rearranges the bishop.
